milestone: Starting a natural history study for CLN5 disease
why_it_matters: A natural history study records how a disease progresses without treatment. Regulators ask for it before trials.

numbers.basis: CLN5 disease and its close relatives

usual_route: FDA draft guidance says prospective natural history studies generally take more time than reusing existing data, and longitudinal ones can be lengthy and costly.
No published figure was found for the time to set up such a study (protocol, ethics approval, sites, funding), so none is stated.

usual_route_source.label: FDA, Rare Diseases: Natural History Studies for Drug Development (2019)

atlas_route: CLN5 disease already has 2 natural history studies registered. Check these first: joining may beat starting a new one.
3 more exist for CLN1 disease, CLN3 disease, CLN6 disease (6A): protocols, outcome measures and teams to learn from and ask to collaborate with.

own_studies.title: A Natural History Study of Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis Type 5 (CLN5)
Natural History and Longitudinal Clinical Assessments in NCL / Batten Disease, the International DEM-CHILD Database

relative_studies.title: Natural History of Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis, Batten's CLN6 Diseae
Natural History Study of Batten Disease
A Retrospective, Natural History Study in Children With CLN2

assumptions: A study for CLN5 disease could reuse outcome measures from its relatives. Not yet validated: clinicians must confirm the diseases are close enough (shared mechanism, different genes).
Durations are those of the registered studies; a new study could be shorter or longer.
No time or cost saving is stated, because there is no cited figure for one.
validate_next: Whether each existing study is still enrolling and open to families with CLN5 disease.
Whether relatives' protocols and registries can be shared (ask the sponsors).
Expert review of how well outcome measures transfer between these diseases.
